checkpoints.description: [2/2] batch summary names skipped requirement checks; 252 tests, 4/4 gates pass
Task 'muse-requirements-visibility' completed successfully.
[1/1] Add batch --retry-unfit: with --resume and --requirements, rerender accepted tracks that miss the limits

impact_assessment.why: A judge-accepted track that misses the requirements stays unfit on every resume unless --force names it
impact_assessment.benefits: One flag rerenders exactly the unfit tracks and reuses the rest
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new opt-in flag, dry-run reason gains 'unfit rerender'; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: reuses existing batch state, no schema change; cost: each rerender is a billed take, only on explicit flag
impact_assessment.mitigation: Flag needs --resume and --requirements; dry-run previews the plan; failing-first tests

checkpoints.description: [1/1] batch --retry-unfit implemented and documented; 256 tests, 4/4 gates pass
Task 'muse-retry-unfit' completed successfully.
[1/2] compose gains an optional fit hook and analysis.requirement_fit maps duration and score misses to retry hints; [2/2] batch retry-on-requirements flag wires it, with tests and docs

impact_assessment.why: The attempts loop retries only on the judge verdict, so a take that is accepted but too short or low-scoring is never retried
impact_assessment.benefits: A batch can spend its attempts on getting tracks to meet the requirements, not only the theme
impact_assessment.risks: contract: compose gets an optional keyword with default None, existing callers unchanged, new opt-in batch flag; dependency: analysis imports types only, no cycle; concurrency: none; state: no schema change; cost: extra billed takes, only with the flag and only for prompt-fixable misses, capped by attempts
impact_assessment.mitigation: Opt-in flag needing a requirements file and attempts above 1; loudness, rate, channels and bit depth never trigger retries; failing-first tests; best take prefers one that fits

checkpoints.description: [1/2] compose fit hook and requirement_fit; 268 tests, 4/4 gates pass
[2/2] batch retry-on-requirements flag wired and documented; 272 tests, 4/4 gates pass
Task 'muse-retry-on-requirements' completed successfully.
[1/2] muse/export.py streams a WAV to mono 16-bit PCM at a chosen rate, with tests; [2/2] muse export subcommand, docs and the Keystone sample-rate caveat

impact_assessment.why: Keystone mixes only clips of one sample rate and reads only mono 16-bit WAV, so real or mock Muse tracks at other rates fail to mix; stdlib cannot convert them today
impact_assessment.benefits: A rendered track becomes loadable and mixable by Keystone with one command, still stdlib only and offline
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new subcommand and new module only, existing commands unchanged; dependency: none, stdlib wave and struct, analysis helper renamed to public pcm_values inside the package; concurrency: output written via temp file and replace; state: never modifies the source audio or muse.json; quality: linear resampling aliases and is fine for game music but not mastering
impact_assessment.mitigation: Streamed in chunks so memory is bounded; source never overwritten; rate range validated; failing-first tests including chunk-size independence; docs state the resampler limits

checkpoints.description: [1/2] export module streams mono 16-bit resampled WAV; 288 tests, 4/4 gates pass
[2/2] muse export subcommand and docs; verified a Keystone load and mix end to end; 4/4 gates pass
Task 'muse-export-wav' completed successfully.

[1/4] Export reports write failures as write failures, creates the output folder and validates chunk size; [2/4] README analyze example checks the exported file; [3/4] sample_rates requirement key and Keystone preset pin 22050 Hz; [4/4] low-pass filter before downsampling, gated by a measured speed and rejection spike

impact_assessment.why: The export review found write errors reported as read errors, a README example that checks the original file, a preset that cannot see the sample rate, and a resampler that aliases tones above the target Nyquist at full level
impact_assessment.benefits: Accurate error messages, a documented workflow that verifies the exported file, a preset check that matches what Keystone can mix, and exported music without false tones
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new optional requirement key and a stricter Keystone preset, so raw tracks at other rates now fail it by design; dependency: stdlib only, older Muse versions reject the new key; concurrency: none; state: no schema change, export stays atomic; quality: a pure Python FIR filter may be slow, so it ships only if it meets the measured budget
impact_assessment.mitigation: Four independent milestones each passing the gates alone; failing-first tests; the filter milestone starts with a spike and a go or no-go measurement; changelog and README state the preset change

checkpoints.description: [1/5] Export reports write failures as write failures, opens the source before creating the output folder, validates chunk size; [2/5] README analyze example checks the exported file; [3/5] retry-unfit skips tracks whose only misses are format limits a rerender cannot change; [4/5] sample_rates key and a separate keystone-mix preset, leaving keystone-audio unchanged; [5/5] low-pass filter before downsampling, 65 taps measured feasible, gated by a go or no-go on the full pipeline

impact_assessment.why: Review of the plan found that pinning the rate in the existing preset would make every raw batch track unfit, and that retry-unfit already rerenders format misses forever, one billed take per run; the filter budget was also unmeasured
impact_assessment.benefits: Accurate export errors, a verifiable workflow, no futile billed rerenders, a preset that matches what Keystone can mix, and exported music without false tones
impact_assessment.risks: contract: retry-unfit stops rerendering format-only misses and says so, new optional requirement key, a new preset file, existing preset unchanged; dependency: stdlib only, older Muse rejects the new key; concurrency: none; state: no schema change, export stays atomic; quality: pure Python polyphase FIR is about 8 s for 3 minutes of filter work plus 3 s baseline, so the budget is 20 s
impact_assessment.mitigation: Five independent milestones each passing the gates alone; failing-first tests; the retry-unfit fix lands before the rate key; the filter milestone ends with a full pipeline timing and a stop if it misses 20 s
